chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani from Sa'd al-Iskaf said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, when the pilgrim takes his travel gear, every step he takes is recorded by Allah as ten good deeds, erases ten bad deeds, and raises him ten degrees, until he finishes his gear. When his mount stands firm, every time it lifts a hoof or places it, Allah records for him the like of that, until he completes his pilgrimage rites. When he completes his rites, Allah forgives him for the remainder of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, and the month of Rabi' al-Awwal. When four months have passed, he mixes with the people.'

key_terms.رَبِيعٍ الْأَوَّلِ: Rabi' al-Awwal (the fourth month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific spiritual rewards for a Muslim during the preparation and travel phase of Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the spiritual merit of Hajj begins with the intention and physical preparation, granting tenfold rewards for every step taken while packing and traveling. This tradition highlights the continuity of reward from the home to the sanctuary, culminating in a unique period of forgiveness extending through the months of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, and Rabi' al-Awwal before the pilgrim fully reintegrates with the community.
